newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Visco urges deal with France over EMU.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Visco urges deal with France over EMU.

text.p: Italy's Minister of Finance Vincenzo Visco said on Wednesday that he shared French concerns over the stability pact on European economic and monetary union (EMU) but stressed that EMU should go head on schedule.
In an interview with Milan daily Corriere della Sera, Visco said that a political solution should be found to ease the concern of France within the framework of the Maastricht Treaty.

He added that French requests for time to consider the EU stability pact were just and understandable. "It is clear that one wants a rebalancing between the technical aspects of convergence and political management," he said.
But he added, "The European train has left. Monetary union will be completed in the set time".
The EMU stability pact was agreed to enforce budgetary rigour in the planned single currency, and limits the budget deficits of countries that enter the euro.
Visco added that stable finances and economic development were not incompatible, but it was clear that economic growth must not come from the expansion of public spending.

Dealers on financial markets on Wednesday said they believed that a compromise would be reached whereby France would agree to the stability pact in return for making employment and economic growth a priority in Europe.
